messages:
anna: Heads-up: I pushed a quick mock for a "role impact preview" in the console — it shows how a chosen role + scope will affect routing policies and quota visibility for that tenant. Need input on the API shape for computing the preview server-side.

mike: Nice. Is this going to calculate effective route affinity and quota precedence? or just UI filters?

anna: Both ideally. We want a lightweight endpoint that returns a compact explanation: which routes are allowed, which quotas apply, and any routing overrides that would trigger fallbacks. Not full evaluation of tokens etc.

sam: Can we avoid evaluating full policy graph for every keystroke? perf will explode for big orgs. Maybe we compute a delta from a baseline and cache common role combos.

liz: +1 on caching. Also need telemetry hooks so we can know which previews were used in rollouts (to link to regressions). We should capture preview_response_version and latency.

rohit: For API: what about POST /rbac/preview with payload { principal, role_ids, scope_ids, context: { region, route } } returning { allowed_routes: [...], quota_buckets: [...], fallbacks: [...] }? Something like that.

mike: That seems fine. Two concerns: 1) we must respect private deployment data boundaries (no tenant secrets in request), and 2) preview must not mutate any state.

anna: Agreed. We'll mark endpoint as read-only and validate inputs. Also add a param ?fast=true to run the cheap path (approximate) vs exact.

sam: For fast=true we can run a heuristics path that uses precomputed routing-affinity indexes and quota summaries. If customer wants exact, queue a background job and return a job_id for the heavier compute. UX can poll that.

liz: UX notes: show badge for "approximate" vs "exact" and drop a tooltip: "Exact previews may take ~30s for large tenants". Also track when people use exact — that will help prioritize performance.

rohit: About telemetry schema: suggest we emit event preview.request with props { mode: "fast|exact", roles_count, scopes_count, duration_ms, result_size, tenant_tier }. Also preview.response. Keep PII out.

anna: sounds good. Can we agree on the response shape? quick draft: 
```json
{
  "allowed_routes": [ { "route": "/v1/generate", "method": "POST", "reason": "role:route:allow" } ],
  "quota_buckets": [ { "name": "daily_tokens", "limit": 1e6, "applies": true, "source": "route_quota" } ],
  "fallbacks": [ { "route": "/v1/generate", "fallback_to": "gpt-lite", "trigger": "quota_exhausted" } ],
  "notes": [ "approximate: uses cached affinity index" ]
}
```

mike: That is workable. A few tweaks: add a "confidence" score on items when mode=fast, and an events array for audit links.

sam: Also return an array of affected_tenants or tenant_sample when admin previewing multi-tenant roles? We need to be careful with data leakage — maybe only counts (e.g., affected_count) unless admin context.

liz: For rollout UX: put this behind a feature flag and gate exact mode to internal + canary tenants first. We'll need a small experiment to see if PMs find it helpful.

anna: plan: I'll implement server endpoint and a thin console view that hits fast=true by default. Exact mode behind flag. Rohit, can you own telemetry schema? Sam, can you sketch caching strategy? Mike, can you sign off on security boundary?

rohit: On it. I'll post schema in #eng-platform-telemetry tomorrow.

sam: I'll prototype cache TTLs and precompute jobs for tenants > 500 routes.

mike: I'll review the threat model later today. Mainly: ensure preview endpoint can't be used to enumerate tenant routes for other customers. Rate-limit and auth checks.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: rbac-preview-service v0.1.0 -> staging (etag: a1b2c3) :rocket:

anna: thanks — moving this to a draft PR. will ping when ready for code review. :thumbsup:
